note: Reconstructed from evals/2026-09-18-probe-doc-headings-claim.md, which was mechanical (contract_sweep.py) and named its own next eval: that a researcher given the reference actually writes the headings it names, and that a dataset probe does not write real rows. The api kind is not in this set — it needs a live credential and real vendor calls, which no harness here can give. The agent is exercised as a proxy: a general-purpose subagent given agents/researcher.md.

evals.name: dataset-probe-statistics-only-and-template-headings
evals.prompt:
You are the dev-team researcher in probe mode. Your six fields:

- Kind: `dataset`
- Source: `readmissions`
- Purpose: the `risk` package's modeling section predicts 30-day readmission; the designer picks the target, the feature set and the split from this document.
- Access: `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.csv`, relative to the plugin directory holding this eval set (the one with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`).
- Extracted skill: `none`
- Output path: `docs/sources/readmissions.md`

Harness rules: write every file you would write — the probe doc, the profile script, the statistics file — into `outputs/`, keeping its repo-relative path (`outputs/docs/sources/...`). Write nothing anywhere else, including scratch files. No scratch venv is needed: `python3` with pandas is on PATH. The Skill tool cannot load this project's skills in this harness, so invoking `planning-templates` means reading `skills/planning-templates/references/source-probe.md` in the plugin directory and recording in `transcript.md` that you read it.
evals.expected_output: a dataset probe doc on the template's headings, with statistics only — no rows, personal columns redacted — and a task-fit section that names the target, the leakage and the split
expectations: outputs/ holds the probe doc, a re-runnable profile script and a statistics file (`readmissions.md`, `readmissions.profile.py`, `readmissions.stats.json`); there is no `.sample.json` anywhere under outputs/

No value from the CSV's `full_name`, `email` or `notes` columns appears anywhere under outputs/, the statistics file included; each of those columns is recorded with its null rate and distinct count and `<redacted>` in place of any example value

The probe doc's `##` headings are the dataset template's, in its order — Access, Provenance, Shape, Observed schema, Duplicates and keys, Target, Leakage, Features, Splitting, Supported tasks, Quirks, Cost and time of a full pass — optionally followed by Sections served (with or without a `## <pkg>/<section>` entry under it); Changes since last probe and Differs from the extracted skill's fixtures are absent, since this is a first probe with no extracted skill; no heading the template does not define
The document opens with the template's three lines: the `# Source probe — readmissions — dataset — <date>` title, a Purpose line, and a Profile/Statistics line
Provenance says `none found`, or says as plainly that the dataset carries no data card, README or column dictionary

Observed schema gives, per column, the dtype as loaded against the declared dtype, the null percentage and the distinct count; `systolic`'s row (or its note) names both of its missing spellings, `n/a` and empty, and its dtype as loaded is reported truthfully — float64 under pandas' default missing-value parsing, which treats `n/a` as null, or object when `n/a` is kept as text — with the doc saying which parsing it used
Duplicates and keys reports the exact-duplicate row count and says `patient_id` is not unique

Target names `readmitted_30d`, gives its class balance and the majority-class baseline rate any model must beat; Leakage names `discharge_code`; Splitting says the split must be chronological on `admitted_at` and grouped by `patient_id`
Quirks names every redacted column and `systolic`'s mixed missing-value spellings (`n/a` and empty)

evals.name: dataset-reprobe-second-section-appends-sections-served-item
evals.prompt:
You are the dev-team researcher in probe mode, spawned by `/dev-team:run-package risk` at the PROBE step for a section whose contract row names a source that already has a probe doc. Your seven fields:

- Kind: `dataset`
- Source: `readmissions`
- Purpose: the `risk` package's `features` section builds the per-admission feature frame — `age`, `region`, `systolic`, `cholesterol` — keyed by `patient_id` and `admitted_at`, for the `model` section to consume; the designer needs each of those columns' loaded dtype, null rate and range, and nothing about the target or the outcome codes.
- Access: `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.csv`, relative to the plugin directory holding this eval set (the one with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`).
- Extracted skill: `none`
- Section: `risk/features`
- Write to: `docs/sources/readmissions.md`

The document at `docs/sources/readmissions.md` already exists: in this harness it is `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.md` in the plugin directory, written on 2026-09-20 for the `risk/model` section. Its profile script and statistics file were not carried into the harness; recompute them.

Harness rules: write every file you would write — the updated probe doc, the profile script, the statistics file — into `outputs/`, keeping its repo-relative path (`outputs/docs/sources/...`). Write nothing anywhere else, including scratch files. No scratch venv is needed: `python3` with pandas is on PATH. The Skill tool cannot load this project's skills in this harness, so invoking `planning-templates` means reading `skills/planning-templates/references/source-probe.md` in the plugin directory, and invoking `git-workflow-and-versioning` means reading `skills/git-workflow-and-versioning/SKILL.md`; record in `transcript.md` that you read each. Where you would run `git add` and `git commit`, do not: write the exact commands you would run — the staged paths and the full commit message with its trailer — to `outputs/commit.txt`, and record the same in `transcript.md`.
evals.expected_output: the existing readmissions probe doc kept whole and refreshed to today's date, with a new `## risk/features` item appended under **Sections served** carrying only the six columns the features purpose needs, no schema change recorded, the model section's task-fit content intact, and a commit with scope `probe readmissions`
expectations: `outputs/docs/sources/readmissions.md` exists and is the fixture document kept, not replaced: every `##` heading of `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.md` is present in the same order, and the `## risk/model` item under **Sections served** is still there with the same nine columns it listed

**Sections served** gains exactly one new `## risk/features` heading, placed after the `## risk/model` item, and its first line after the heading states the purpose it was probed for (the features section's contract purpose from the prompt)

The `## risk/features` item lists only the columns the features purpose needs — `patient_id`, `admitted_at`, `age`, `region`, `systolic`, `cholesterol` — each with its loaded dtype, null rate or range, and an `observed` label; it does not name `readmitted_30d`, `discharge_code`, `full_name`, `email`, `notes` or `site_version`
The title line reads `# Source probe — readmissions — dataset — <date>` where `<date>` is the run's date, not 2026-09-20, and the Purpose and Profile/Statistics preamble lines still follow it

**Changes since last probe** is either absent or records no change to the observed schema (`none` or the equivalent): no column is reported added, removed, retyped, or with a different null rate or distinct count, because the data is the same file the 2026-09-20 probe profiled

The task-fit headings keep the first probe's content: **Target** still names `readmitted_30d` with the 89.4% majority-class baseline, **Leakage** still names `discharge_code`, **Splitting** still says chronological on `admitted_at` and grouped by `patient_id`; none of Target, Leakage, Features, Splitting or Supported tasks reads `not a modeling task`

`outputs/commit.txt` records a commit whose message summary begins `probe readmissions:` (scope `probe <source>`), stages only `docs/sources/readmissions.*` paths by explicit path, and carries one `Dev-Team-Run:` trailer; neither `transcript.md` nor the final message says the run does not commit because no `Commit: yes` field was given

outputs/ also holds `readmissions.profile.py` and `readmissions.stats.json` beside the doc; no value from the CSV's `full_name`, `email` or `notes` columns appears anywhere under outputs/, and there is no `.sample.json` anywhere under outputs/

The return (the final message in `transcript.md`) is ten lines or fewer and gives the access status, the rows and columns profiled, whether it was a sample, the discrepancy count, the path, and the commit

evals.name: dataset-reprobe-second-section-keeps-shared-lines-byte-for-byte
evals.prompt:
You are the dev-team researcher in probe mode, spawned by `/dev-team:run-package risk` at the PROBE step for a section whose contract row names a source that already has a probe doc. Your eight fields:

- Kind: `dataset`
- Source: `readmissions`
- Purpose: the `risk` package's `slices` section reports the model's recall and precision per slice — per `region`, and per calendar quarter of `admitted_at` — and suppresses a slice with too few positives; the designer needs the region levels as they are spelled, the quarters the data spans, and the row count and the count of `readmitted_30d = 1` rows in each slice, and nothing about the features or the split.
- Access: `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.csv`, relative to the plugin directory holding this eval set (the one with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and an `evals/` directory).
- Extracted skill: `none`
- Section: `risk/slices`
- Write to: `docs/sources/readmissions.md`
- Run: `run-package risk`

The document at `docs/sources/readmissions.md` already exists: in this harness it is `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.md` in the plugin directory holding this eval set, written on 2026-09-20 for the `risk/model` section. Its profile script and statistics file were not carried into the harness; recompute them.

Harness rules: write every file you would write — the updated probe doc, the profile script, the statistics file — into `outputs/`, keeping its repo-relative path (`outputs/docs/sources/...`). Write nothing anywhere else, including scratch files. No scratch venv is needed: `python3` with pandas is on PATH. The Skill tool cannot load this project's skills in this harness, so invoking `planning-templates` means reading `skills/planning-templates/references/source-probe.md` under your plugin root, and invoking `git-workflow-and-versioning` means reading `skills/git-workflow-and-versioning/SKILL.md` under your plugin root; record in `transcript.md` that you read each. Where you would run `git add` and `git commit`, do not: write the exact commands you would run — the staged paths and the full commit message with its trailer — to `outputs/commit.txt`, and record the same in `transcript.md`.
evals.expected_output: the fixture probe doc with only its title date changed and one `## risk/slices` entry appended (plus, at most, added lines for new facts): every line of the shared body and the `## risk/model` entry byte for byte as the 2026-09-20 probe left them, and no **Changes since last probe**
expectations: `outputs/docs/sources/readmissions.md` exists, and every non-blank line of the fixture `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.md` from its `## Access` heading through its `## Sections served` heading is present in it byte for byte and in the same order: no fixture line in that span is reworded, re-wrapped, re-ordered or dropped, and no table row has a cell changed (a line-by-line diff of the two files shows only added lines there, or none)

The two preamble lines under the title are the fixture's, byte for byte: the `Purpose:` line is still the one written for the `model` section (it does not name `slices` and is not replaced or extended with this run's purpose), and the `Profile: readmissions.profile.py · Statistics: readmissions.stats.json` line is unchanged
The title line reads `# Source probe — readmissions — dataset — <date>` where `<date>` is the run's date, not 2026-09-20, and is otherwise the fixture's title line
The `## risk/model` entry under **Sections served** is the fixture's, byte for byte: its heading, its two `Purpose:` lines, and its table's header and all nine column rows

**Sections served** gains exactly one new heading, `## risk/slices`, placed after the whole `## risk/model` entry; the first line after the heading states the purpose it was probed for (the slices section's purpose from the prompt); the entry lists `region`, `admitted_at` and `readmitted_30d`, each labelled `observed`, and does not list `age`, `systolic`, `cholesterol`, `site_version`, `full_name`, `email` or `notes`

The count of `readmitted_30d = 1` rows per region (east 4, north 4, south 10, west 8) and per calendar quarter (2025 Q1 9, Q2 3, Q3 6, Q4 7, 2026 Q1 1) is in the document, either inside the `## risk/slices` entry or as lines added under an existing heading after the lines already there; none of it is written into a line the fixture already had — the `region`, `admitted_at` and `readmitted_30d` rows of the **Observed schema** table and the paragraph under **Target** are the fixture's, character for character

The phrase `Changes since last probe` appears nowhere in `outputs/docs/sources/readmissions.md`, as a heading or as a line: no line was rewritten, and the added entry and any added line are not recorded as changes

outputs/ holds `docs/sources/readmissions.profile.py` and `docs/sources/readmissions.stats.json` beside the doc, and the statistics file carries this run's numbers for the 246 rows, `region`, `admitted_at` and `readmitted_30d` among its columns
`transcript.md` shows the profile script was run against `readmissions.csv` in this run, before the doc was written: the shared lines were kept after a real re-probe, not by skipping it
